1: Oh, no! The humans are coming to steal your dino eggs! Quick, click on a dino from the menu on the right, then click in the playable area to place the dino to defend your nest!
2: Good start! Click one of your dinos to see upgrades. Stronger bites, faster attacks, and wider range can keep those egg-snatching humans away from the nest!
3: Uh oh, Nest Runners are sprinting in! Place dinos where the path bends so they can chomp at humans for as long as possible.
4: Remember, dinos cannot defend the nest if they are staring at empty grass. Range circles show where each dino can attack.
5: Wardens are marching in with heavier gear! They move slower, but if they reach the nest, they steal more eggs than the little scouts.
6: Try mixing dinos instead of buying only one favorite. The humans evolved alongside dinos, so they brought tricks for every kind of defender.
7: Need to change your plan? Click a placed dino and sell it to recover some money, then rebuild before the next human rush begins.
8: Parasaurolophus can help the nest economy. It may not fight much, but its calls bring in money for more defenders.
9: Tiny Compy Packs are rushing the nest! Fast attackers like Velociraptor can help catch enemies that slip through slow heavy hits.
10: Dilophosaurus boosts nearby dinos with an attack speed aura. Place damage dealers inside its range and let the whole pack get louder.
12: Ankylosaurus can slow humans with heavy hits. Slowed enemies spend more time inside your defenses, which means more chances to stop them.
13: Raptor Riders are here! The humans learned the hard way that riding dinos is faster than running from them.
15: Some upgrade paths change how a dino behaves, not just its damage. Read the buttons before spending your hard-earned nest money.
17: Egg Cart Caravans are rolling toward the nest! They are slow, sturdy, and very bad news if they reach your eggs.
18: Oviraptor can aim at one chosen spot. Use Set Target near a busy bend to rain trouble on humans before they reach the nest.
19: Bone Doctors have arrived! These humans patch themselves up, so focus them quickly before they undo your dinos' hard work.
22: Pteranodon can move after placement. If the human path pressure changes, lift it to a better perch when its cooldown is ready.
24: Troodon helps nearby towers target the weakest enemies. That is perfect for cleaning up humans trying to sneak away with one egg too many.
25: Shieldback Raiders are carrying armor now! Bigger damage, pierce, splash, and smart upgrades can crack through their defenses.
27: Trike Ram Teams hit the nest hard if they break through. Do not let their slow march fool you; these humans came prepared.
30: Allosaurus attacks in bursts. If a wave arrives in clumps, burst damage can tear open a crowd before it spreads out.
34: Spinosaurus can pierce through lines of enemies, while Sarcosuchus can splash groups. Long straight paths and packed bends are their favorite hunting grounds.
37: Nest Smoke Shamans are boosting nearby humans! Their smoke makes the raid faster and weakens your slows, so bring them down quickly.
39: Armored Ankylosaurs have joined the raid. The humans keep copying dino strength, which is rude, dangerous, and honestly pretty bold.
41: Ballista Crews are rolling in with heavy weapons. Keep upgrading your main defenders before the nest becomes target practice.
45: By now your defense should have a plan: damage to kill, support to boost, control to slow, and economy to afford the next panic.
49: Chrome-Claw Raptors are fast and partly armored. If they blur past your heavy hitters, add faster attacks or better coverage.
51: Ironcrest Triceratops are huge, armored, and stubborn. The humans are getting desperate to reach the eggs first.
55: Late waves punish weak spots. Watch where enemies survive the longest, then upgrade or reposition dinos to cover that stretch.
61: Bio-Surgeon Doctors are here! They heal nearby humans, so do not let them stand safely behind the rest of the raid.
63: Robo Raptors are loose! The humans built metal runners because regular bad ideas were apparently not enough.
68: If fast enemies keep escaping, try aura support, fast towers, or manual targeting near the exit before they reach the nest.
73: Robo Stego Bulwarks are massive armored walls. Splash damage is reduced against them, so focused single-target power matters more now.
80: The humans are mixing healers, armor, speed, and machines. Your defense needs layers too: slow them, boost allies, and finish weak targets.
85: Eggbreaker Titans have arrived. These giant egg thieves hit the nest brutally hard, so pour damage into them before they cross the final stretch.
92: At this point, every upgrade choice matters. Spend money where enemies are actually breaking through, not where the nest already feels safe.
100: Round 100! The humans have turned this egg raid into a full war, but your dinos have defended the nest for a century of waves.
110: The final stretch is about endurance. Keep checking cooldowns, aura coverage, weak lanes, and whether your biggest damage dealers are fully upgraded.
120: This is the last planned raid for now. Every dino, every upgrade, every roar: protect the eggs and send the humans home empty-handed!
